questions.q: What distinguishes buy-side firms from sell-side firms?
options: Buy-side firms manage money on behalf of their own or clients' capital; sell-side firms facilitate markets for clients
Buy-side firms only trade bonds; sell-side firms only trade equities
Buy-side firms are always larger than sell-side firms
There is no meaningful difference between the two
questions.explain: Buy-side firms (asset managers, pension funds, hedge funds) manage capital to generate returns, while sell-side firms (banks, broker-dealers) facilitate markets, earning revenue from spreads, fees, and commissions.

questions.q: Which hedge fund strategy uses quantitative models to find many small, short-term pricing relationships between related instruments?
options: Global macro
Event-driven
Statistical arbitrage
Long-only indexing
questions.explain: Statistical arbitrage identifies many small, short-term pricing relationships using quantitative models and trades them systematically at scale.

questions.q: How does a proprietary trading firm differ from a hedge fund?
options: A prop trading firm trades its own capital with no outside investors, while a hedge fund manages outside investors' money
A prop trading firm can only trade commodities
A hedge fund never charges any fees
There is no practical difference between the two
questions.explain: Proprietary trading firms trade the firm's own capital with no fund-raising or investor reporting, which is a fundamentally different business model from a hedge fund that exists to manage outside investors' money.

questions.q: What does a typical asset manager or pension fund mandate look like compared to a hedge fund?
options: Identical in every respect to a hedge fund's strategy
Usually long-only and benchmarked against an index, aiming to match or beat that benchmark
Always market-neutral and benchmark-free
Exclusively focused on short-term statistical arbitrage
questions.explain: Asset managers and pension funds typically run long-only mandates benchmarked against an index such as the S&P 500, rather than the more varied, often market-neutral strategies common at hedge funds.

questions.q: What is the primary role of a bank's trading desk on the sell-side?
options: Exclusively managing the bank's own pension fund
Servicing client order flow, providing liquidity, and structuring products, alongside some proprietary risk within regulatory limits
Running statistical arbitrage strategies for outside investors only
Acting as a central clearinghouse for derivatives
questions.explain: A bank trading desk primarily services client flow — executing trades and providing liquidity — while also taking on limited proprietary risk, constrained by rules like the Volcker Rule.
